message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each except one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score **1,000 points** (or a pre‑agreed target). Points are tallied after each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you may play **one** card that matches either the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard. 3. If you cannot play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise, you can be challenged.) | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your **second‑to‑last** card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score. | | **Variations** | • **Stacking** – allow Draw Two/Wild Draw Four to be stacked on top of each other.
• **Custom Rules** – e.g., “Draw Two” can be played on any card, “Reverse” can be played on any card, etc. Always agree on variations before starting. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of colors** – try to hold onto a single color so you can play more cards later. 2. **Use Wilds strategically** – save them for when you’re stuck or to change the color to your advantage. 3. **Watch opponents** – if someone is close to UNO, they might be holding a Wild Draw Four; be ready to challenge if you suspect a rule violation. 4. **Play fast** – Uno is meant to be a quick, lively game; keep the pace brisk. Enjoy your game!
